Why do we still care about Big O Notation in 2026 when computers are so fast? 🚀

Because inefficient code scales terribly. 

Here is the ultimate breakdown of Time & Space Complexity:
🔹 O(1) - Constant: The dream. Array lookups.
🔹 O(log n) - Logarithmic: The standard. Binary search.
🔹 O(n) - Linear: The baseline. Simple loops.
🔹 O(n^2) - Quadratic: The danger zone. Nested loops.

Builder's Angle 🛠️: When I optimize embedded C code for microcontrollers with limited RAM, jumping from O(n^2) to O(n log n) isn't just a "nice to have"—it prevents the entire hardware system from crashing.

What is the worst time complexity you've ever seen make it into production? 👇
